question: Can a class-balanced, cross-validation-tuned LightGBM model beat a standard radial-basis-function neural network at flagging risky cases on the public German credit dataset?
method: Stratified 70/30 split (seed 42); preprocessing fit on train only; baseline RBF net and improved LightGBM tuned by 3-fold CV on train; test set used once; seeds 42-44.
baseline: Standard RBF network: k-means centres, Gaussian RBF activations, logistic-regression output; number of centres and width chosen by CV on train.
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM with hyperparameters tuned by randomized CV search on train and sigmoid-calibrated probabilities.
notes: German credit is a stand-in for the paper's IT-risk data, not the paper's own dataset. Predictions use the default 0.5 threshold (argmax). The test set has only ~300 rows, so differences are noisy. Seeds vary model randomness only; the split is fixed.
